outline_action: Search specifically for validated LC-MS/MS or NMR protocols for inosine and SCFAs in serum or tissue samples. Look for consensus statements from metabolomics societies (e.g., MSI) regarding absolute quantification standards in blood/tissue. Compare urine-based validation parameters with existing serum method requirements to identify matrix-specific gaps (e.g., protein interference, stability).
remaining_gap: This study validates inosine quantification in urine, not serum or tumor microenvironment (TME). It does not address short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) at all. No consensus guidelines for absolute concentration measurement of inosine or SCFAs specifically in serum/TME were identified in this text. The physiological concentration ranges provided are urine-specific (creatinine-normalized) and cannot be directly extrapolated to serum/TME standards.
